The first lady unveiled her new “PhotoArchival Digital Edition” over the weekend to coincide with the release of her widely panned Amazon Prime Video docuseries, “Melania: The Series,” a follow-up to her similarly poorly reviewed documentary, “Melania.”

For $150, customers receive “a digital album delivered as a movie file.”

The product listing on Trump’s website features two photographs — one of her sitting in a chair, the other posing beside a movie clapperboard.

Promotional material describes the release as “an exclusive collection of digital photographs by internationally acclaimed fashion photographer Ellen von Unwerth.” It adds, “The collection presents a visual portrait of Mrs. Trump, showcasing von Unwerth’s distinctive artistry.”

Guardian columnist Arwa Mahdawi delivered a scathing assessment of the offering in a column published Tuesday.

“All I’m saying is that for $150, I’d expect a bit more of Von Unwerth’s signature style,” she wrote, adding: “The first lady just looks how she always looks to me: like a Madame Tussauds waxwork figure who was brought to life by an evil sorcerer.”

Referencing Trump’s new $90 Christmas ornament, another addition to her merchandise range, Mahdawi quipped: “I suppose it is holiday grifting season.”

The reaction on social media was similarly unenthusiastic, with critics suggesting “the grift never ends.”
